'''Agata Shrine''' (縣神社, Agata Jinja) is an {{ill|Independent Shinto shrine|ja|単立神社|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q7882536|redirects to 単立|2=ja|3=単立|2=ja|3=単立|redirects to 単立|2=ja|3=単立|}} located in {{ill|Hagiwara-chō|ja|萩原町|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11620353}}, {{ill|Gero, Gifu|en|Gero, Gifu|qid=Q819639|lt=Gero City}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Gifu|af|Gifu-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Gifu|ar|غيفو (محافظة)|arz|جيفو (محافظه)|az|Gifu prefekturası|azb|قیفو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Gifu|be|Гіфу (прэфектура)|bg|Гифу|bn|গিফু প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Gifu|cdo|Gifu-gâing|ce|Гифу (префектура)|ceb|Gifu-ken|ckb|پارێزگای گیفو|cs|Prefektura Gifu|cy|Gifu (talaith)|da|Gifu-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Gifu|eo|Gubernio Gifu|es|Prefectura de Gifu|et|Gifu prefektuur|eu|Gifu (prefektura)|fa|استان گیفو|fi|Gifun prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Gifu|frr|Gifu (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Gifu|gl|Prefectura de Gifu|hak|Gifu-yen|he|גיפו (מחוז)|hr|Gifu (prefektura)|hu|Gifu prefektúra|hy|Գիֆու (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Gifu|ilo|Prepektura ti Gifu|it|Prefettura di Gifu|ja|岐阜県|jv|Préfèktur Gifu|ka|გიფუს პრეფექტურა|kn|ಗಿಫು (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|기후현|lt|Gifu prefektūra|lv|Gifu prefektūra|mk|Гифу (префектура)|mni|ꯒꯤꯐꯨ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|गिफू प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Gifu|ne|गिफु|nl|Gifu (prefectuur)|no|Gifu (prefektur)|nov|Gifu Prefekture|os|Гифу (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Gifu|pl|Prefektura Gifu|pnb|ضلع گیفو|pt|Gifu|ro|Prefectura Gifu|ru|Гифу (префектура)|se|Gifu prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Gifu|simple|Gifu Prefecture|sk|Gifu (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Гифу|su|Préféktur Gifu|sv|Gifu prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Gifu|tg|Префектураи Гифу|th|จังหวัดกิฟุ|tl|Prepektura ng Gifu|tr|Gifu (prefektörlük)|tt|Гифу (префектура)|uk|Префектура Ґіфу|ur|گیفو پریفیکچر|vi|Gifu|war|Gifu (prefektura)|wuu|岐阜县|zh|岐阜县|zh_classical|岐阜縣|zh_min_nan|Gihu-koān|zh_yue|岐阜縣|qid=Q131277|lt=Gifu Prefecture}}. Its former shrine Rank was a village shrine.
== Deities ==
* Main deity: {{ill|Toshigami|ja|御歳神|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q3028663}}
* Enshrined Deities: {{ill|Ietsumiko no Kami|ja|家津御子神|qid=Q140445993}} (also known as Ietsumiko no Kami), {{ill|Kumano Kusu no Mi no Mikoto|ja|熊野久須美命|qid=Q140445994}} (also known as Kumano Musubi no Kami), {{ill|Kumano Gongen|ja|速玉男命|lt=Hayatama no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素戔嗚命|qid=Q272993}}, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|ja|大山祇神|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q386563}}
== History ==
The sacred object is a naturally shaped stone resembling a mountain. The shrine is situated nearly in the center of the rice field area of the Sakurabuchi alluvial fan. According to the shrine’s historical records, "Since the beginning of land development, the villagers designated this central site as a place for ceremonial plowing and rope laying, eventually enshrining Ootoshikami, the guardian deity of rice fields and grains."
The area surrounding the shrine is the {{ill|Kanda Site|ja|神田遺跡|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135502222}}, a Jomon-period archaeological site where numerous stone tools and Jomon pottery have been excavated. During an excavation in 1973 (Showa 48), dwelling remains and human bones were also discovered.
== Timeline ==
* Founded: Unknown
* 1690 (Genroku 3): Rebuilt
* 1872 (Meiji 5): Designated as a village shrine
* 1908 (Meiji 41): Enshrined four other shrines within the Sakurabuchi area—Kumano Shrine, Tenno Shrine, and two Yama Shrines.
* 1952 (Showa 27): Became a religious corporation as Agata Shrine.
